terms.gloss: from thread and needle: in every detail
terms.grammar: ab with the ablative of acia, sewing thread, and acus, needle
evidence: Traupman 98: ab aciā et acū mihi omnia exposuit
terms.comment: Literally “from the thread and the needle”, of telling every last detail. Lewis & Short has acia (Titinius, Celsus) and acus, but not the phrase, and it is not in the loci collections. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

phrases.latin: Ab aciā et acū mihi omnia exposuit.
phrases.english: He explained everything to me from A to Z.

sources: Lewis & Short: acia · Lewis & Short: acus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 98, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).: p. 319.
